skills.name: Effects of atmospheric pressure on boiling points and on health

note.text:
Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude: there is less air above you.
Boiling point depends on pressure: a liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the pressure above it.
• Lower pressure (high places such as Mount Cameroon) → water boils below 100 °C, so food takes longer to cook.
• Higher pressure (pressure cooker) → water boils above 100 °C, so food cooks faster.
Health: at high altitude there is less oxygen per breath (altitude sickness, headaches, breathlessness); ears 'pop' when pressure changes quickly; divers who rise too fast suffer the bends. Aircraft cabins are pressurised.

sections.heading: Less air higher up
sections.text:
The higher you go, the less air there is above you, so the atmospheric pressure is lower. At the top of Mount Cameroon (about {4000} m) it is roughly two-thirds of the pressure in Douala.
Pressure changes affect boiling, breathing and our ears.

sections.heading: Boiling and pressure
sections.text:
Water boils when its vapour can push back against the pressure of the air above it. With less air pressure, this happens at a lower temperature.
So on a high mountain water may boil at about {90} °C, and food takes longer to cook.
A pressure cooker does the opposite: it traps steam, raises the pressure and makes water boil at about {120} °C, so beans and meat cook much faster. Its safety valve releases steam if the pressure gets too high.

sections.heading: Pressure and health
sections.text:
• At high altitude each breath holds less oxygen: climbers can get headaches, dizziness and breathlessness (altitude sickness).
• Quick changes of pressure, in a plane or a car going down a hill, make your ears 'pop'; swallowing helps.
• Divers who come up too fast can get the bends. Aircraft cabins are pressurised so passengers breathe comfortably.

worked_example.problem: Why do climbers on Mount Cameroon find that rice cooks slowly near the summit?
steps: The air pressure is lower high up.
Lower pressure lowers the boiling point of water below {100} °C.
The water boils at a lower temperature, so the rice cooks more slowly.
worked_example.answer: Lower pressure, lower boiling point, slower cooking

pick.q: Why do some climbers feel dizzy near the summit of a high mountain?
pick.r: The low air pressure means less oxygen in each breath
e: There is less oxygen per breath.
Blood density does not change.
Distance to the sun is not the cause.
pick.y: Altitude sickness comes from low pressure and less oxygen.

pick.q: Why do your ears 'pop' when a plane takes off?
pick.r: The outside pressure changes quickly and the pressure in the middle ear adjusts
w: The engine noise is too loud
e: Noise does not cause popping.
Cabins are warm.
It is about pressure, not oxygen.
pick.y: Swallowing lets air in or out to balance the pressure on the eardrum.

pick.r: At cruising height the air pressure is too low for people to breathe comfortably
e: Pressurising does not add useful weight.
Heating is a separate system.
Engines take in outside air.
pick.y: High up, the outside pressure is too low for healthy breathing.

questions.prompt: Put the explanation in order: why does rice cook slowly near the top of Mount Cameroon?

items.text: The climber is very high up.
There is less air above, so the air pressure is lower.
Water boils at a temperature below 100 °C.
The boiling water is not as hot, so the rice cooks more slowly.

questions.hint: Start from the height and end with the cooking.
